stage: development algorithm comparison, not independent population validation
algorithm: Quadratic plus offsets across gaps >0.5 d, without flux clipping.
Original and detrended top 3 LS peaks plus original/detrended BLS winners; test half, original and double within 0.05–8 d.
Two rounds of local frequency refinement using full-data phase templates.
96-bin periodic interpolation; alternate cycles train/predict each other. Gain >=20%, both folds >=10%, coverage >=80%, at least 3 cycles. These scores are not calibrated false-alarm probabilities.
Choose the highest-gain refinement within each alias; prefer its half alias only within 2 percentage points of its gain.
Narrow dip with secondary noise proxy below 5 or unresolved half-cycle difference retains orbital ambiguity.
Match every supported candidate across all epochs within 1%; nonharmonic alternatives preserve ambiguity.
Auxiliary periodic correlation |r|>=0.8 and predictive gain >=20%, or SAP disagreement, causes source-review status. Correlation is not proof of instrumental origin.
Existing pixel localization checks supplied TPF data and known neighbors. No new catalog lookup is required for offline decisions.
Preserve the original v2 search, refinement, detrending and normal alternating-cycle qualification.

For otherwise unqualified eclipse-shaped candidates with insufficient training phase coverage, >=3 periods of baseline and no boundary flag: leave one observed cycle out at a time; require total gain>=0.20, every training template coverage>=0.80 and at least three held cycles with gain>=0.10. Keep all partial/negative cycles in the total statistic.
Treat integer period ratios 1..8 within1.5% as harmonic families; choose the smallest integer alias within0.02 of best gain, keeping maximum gain within a peak.

For every pair of nonharmonic qualified periods, subtract the full-data base template and test the trial against that residual. Retain a competing group only if residual gain>=0.20, fold gains>=0.10, coverage>=0.80 and gain times residual/original weighted squared flux>=0.05 in every epoch. These diagnostics do not prove separate physical modes.
Do not average away cross-epoch preference for different integer aliases; retain periodic detection but abstain on final period.
Preserve auxiliary/source caution and equal-eclipse orbital ambiguity. No new target discovery or official submission.
metrics: preferred cycle accuracy (1%); abstentions stay in the denominator
photometric P/2 recovery of equal eclipses separately from orbital ambiguity
source cautions, confirmed-variable count always zero
per-case old/new outcomes, all errors and unavailable inputs
limitations: Development thresholds are motivated by observed v1 failures and software fixtures, not learned from an untouched test sample.
Both candidate search and refinement reuse the cross-cycle data; no frequentist significance claim.
No independently labeled quiet real-star negatives yet; population false-positive rate unavailable.
Results and input hashes from v1 must remain unchanged.
LOCO and alternate-cycle scores differ; used only under the predeclared low-coverage eclipse fallback. Selection effect is not calibrated.
Phase templates and detrending remain approximate. Formal period errors, joint baseline fitting, calibrated photometry and real quiet controls are unfinished.
No fresh independent v3 evaluation is implied by this development comparison.
